sources.title: Deterministic modelling of seed dispersal based on observed behaviours of an endemic primate in Brazil
sources.locator: Abstract; Methods, study sites and primate groups; Results, Colônia study site and Model of Seed Transfer.
sources.scope: Primary field study and deterministic seed-dispersal model focused on Leontopithecus chrysomelas in southern Bahia, Brazil; fieldwork on one Colônia group was conducted in 2015–2016, with movement records from two Una Biological Reserve groups taken from a separate 2006 study.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution License, stated in the article copyright statement; the article does not specify a numbered version.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Copyright statement after the article citation; Creative Commons Attribution License.
sources.attribution: Raghunathan N, François L, Cazetta E, Pitance J-L, De Vleeschouwer K, Hambuckers A (2020). Deterministic modelling of seed dispersal based on observed behaviours of an endemic primate in Brazil. PLoS ONE 15(12):e0244220. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0244220. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The field study focused on one Colônia group in southern Bahia, observed over 26 complete days during the Pourouma fruiting season; movement records from two groups at Una Biological Reserve came from a separate 2006 study and supplied 46 and 50 complete observation days.
claims.scope: Three study groups at two nearby Brazilian sites, with data collected in different years and for different purposes.

claims.text: For the Colônia group, the seasonal average daily path was about 1,867 m, and observed Pourouma seeds were dispersed an average of 111 m from parent trees.
claims.scope: Observed values for one group at one site during one fruiting season; not a species-wide movement or dispersal estimate.

claims.text: The MOST model reproduced observed movement and seed-deposition patterns approximately, but seed-deposition outputs were sensitive to selected mature-fruit and feeding-distance thresholds.
claims.scope: Model performance and sensitivity within the study area; not a measurement of regional forest regeneration.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
The study does not establish range-wide ecology, population size, current conservation status, or a general species-wide seed-dispersal effect.
